facts.text: Humanoid-Base-v0 is registered with entry point humanoid.tasks.base_env:BaseEnv and BaseEnvCfg as its env_cfg_entry_point
BaseEnv subclasses DirectRLEnv, the Isaac Lab direct reinforcement-learning environment class
The default scene has four environments (num_envs=4) with 10.0 m spacing
The physics simulation runs with dt = 1/120 s and render_interval = 4
BaseEnvCfg sets decimation = 4
BaseEnv sets self.dt = cfg.sim.dt * cfg.decimation, so its control timestep follows from those two settings
BaseEnvCfg sets episode_length_s = 0.5
BaseEnvCfg sets action_scale = 1
BaseEnvCfg sets num_actions = 50 and action_space = num_actions
BaseEnvCfg sets num_observations = 99 and observation_space = num_observations
_apply_action multiplies the action by cfg.action_scale, clamps it to the robot's soft joint position limits and writes it as the joint position target
_get_dones compares the episode length buffer with max_episode_length and returns the same tensor as terminated and truncated
BaseEnv._get_rewards is empty, so the base environment defines no reward term

_get_observations returns a dictionary with rgb, fixed_rgb, fixed_d, left_hand_rgb, right_hand_rgb, qpos, qvel, action, left/right end-effector poses and targets, finger tip positions and hand contact forces
The left-eye and right-eye RGB images are concatenated along the width dimension (dim=2)
The left-eye and right-eye cameras are 360 x 640 and capture rgb and distance_to_image_plane
The main, left-hand and right-hand cameras are 720 x 1280 and capture rgb and distance_to_image_plane
The default robot is the H1 Inspire configuration (H1_INSPIRE_CFG) with separate left/right arm and hand configs
BaseEnvCfg enables object randomization with randomize = True, randomize_range = 1.0 and randomize_idx = -1
The random agent creates the environment with gym.make(task, cfg=env_cfg), resets it and drives it with env.step
The random agent samples actions uniformly in [-1, 1) using env.action_space.shape
The benchmark targets IsaacLab 1.2.0 and IsaacSim 4.2.0
The asset data is hosted on Hugging Face, outside the clone
The humanoid.tasks extension is installed editable with the Isaac Lab Python
Humanoid-Close-Drawer-v0 is registered with entry point humanoid.tasks.close_drawer:CloseDrawerEnv
CloseDrawerEnv subclasses BaseEnv
Humanoid-Flip-Mug-v0 is registered with entry point humanoid.tasks.flip_mug:FlipMugEnv
FlipMugEnv subclasses BaseEnv
Humanoid-Insert-And-Unload-Cans-v0 is registered with entry point humanoid.tasks.insert_and_unload_cans:InsertAndUnloadCansEnv
InsertAndUnloadCansEnv subclasses BaseEnv
Humanoid-Insert-Cans-v0 is registered with entry point humanoid.tasks.insert_cans:InsertCansEnv
InsertCansEnv subclasses BaseEnv

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds the fake's Python random generator, so one seed and action sequence repeat the fake's trajectory; upstream Isaac Lab seeds torch and its own generators and randomizes the object poses, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two

gaps: the package's fake is kinematic (F0): it writes the action vector to joint positions directly and models no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuators, sensors, noise or camera rendering, so it cannot reproduce Isaac Lab/PhysX behaviour

camera observations are placeholder 1 x 1 arrays: the upstream left-eye and right-eye cameras are 360 x 640 rgb and are concatenated along the width (360 x 1280), and the main, left-hand and right-hand cameras are 720 x 1280 rgb plus distance_to_image_plane (base_env.py:63-112, :257-259)

the fake returns the 16 observation keys of BaseEnv._get_observations with placeholder values; the upstream qpos/qvel lengths, end-effector poses, finger tips and contact forces come from the H1 assets and PhysX, which the clone does not contain

only Humanoid-Base-v0 is served: the other registered task environments (Close-Drawer, Flip-Mug, Insert-Cans, Insert-And-Unload-Cans and the rest) are not bound, and their objects, rewards, success terms and randomization are not modelled
the USD assets are hosted on Hugging Face and the clone has no Isaac Sim 4.2 or Isaac Lab 1.2.0 runtime (README.md:17, :23), so no upstream run was made and the fake was never compared with it
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
BaseEnv itself defines no reward (_get_rewards is empty) and reports the timeout as both terminated and truncated; the fake mirrors that and returns reward 0
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
